decisions.reason: Redesigning the document-field setup does not change the required style-system coverage across the template set.
The field-architecture redesign does not determine or change the templates' default language.
The source requests a more robust field setup but does not specify a visual cue or resolve the existing uncertainty about grey editable-field cues.
Interactive-field architecture is independent of bullet appearance, scaling, alignment, and color requirements.
A more robust field implementation may support formatting preservation, but the source does not change the existing requirement that Title-field formatting be preserved.
The architectural redesign does not change the required trigger or behavior for clearing placeholder text.
The source concerns document-field implementation and does not alter legacy-content paste behavior or resolve the paste-workflow ambiguity.
Redesigning interactive fields does not change table containment or right-hand column positioning after paste.
The field-setup redesign does not change the requirement for reliable manual line breaks after legacy-content pasting.
The source does not modify style prefixes, naming coverage, naming conditions, or style-name language.
Document-field architecture is independent of Tab-driven list hierarchy and alignment behavior.
The requested field redesign remains subject to the existing Word for Windows reliability constraint but does not change that constraint's state.
